events.description: With sensor version 7.11, CrowdStrike introduced the new IPC Template Type, delivered as Rapid Response Content via Channel File 291. Its definition expected 21 input fields, but the sensor code supplied only 20 input values.

events.time: During sensor 7.11 development and release testing (before the release, no fault triggered)
events.description: Manual and automated functional testing was performed using 12 static test cases with a wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field; a stress test passed and the IPC Template Type was validated for use. No fault was triggered.
The first IPC Template Instances were released to production as part of a Rapid Response Content update; these used wildcard matching for the 21st input and deployed successfully.
Two additional IPC Template Instances were deployed, one introducing a non-wildcard matching criterion for the 21st input, resulting in a new version of Channel File 291.
The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances based on the expectation of 21 inputs and passed them; the new channel file was sent to sensors.

events.time: July 19, 2024 (at next IPC notification after receipt)
events.description: Windows sensors receiving the new Channel File 291 evaluated the Template Instances, attempted to access the 21st input value that was not supplied, produced an out-of-bounds memory read, and the system crashed with a PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA bugcheck in csagent.sys.

events.time: As of July 29, 2024 at 5 p.m. PT
events.description: Recovery status: using week-over-week comparison, approximately 99% of Windows sensors were back online compared to before the content update (typical variance is about 1%).
